evidence: Firmware image was erased, written at offset 0x0, and verified with esptool 5.0.2.
Runtime reported MicroPython 1.23.0 and octal SPIRAM with approximately 8.3 MiB free heap on the blank image.
A sanitized reconstruction of the public v0.13 release and captured protected fixture was installed before the first OTA.
The v0.13-to-v0.14 OTA preserved the hardware selector, settings migration, logs, selected app, and user files.
Installed version remained uncommitted until the candidate completed a healthy IDE boot.
The physical device verified five critical package hashes from the final CI artifact.
Seventeen compiled modules loaded successfully on the pinned MicroPython 1.23 runtime.
The operator confirmed correct red, green, blue, white, and black output on the exact final candidate.
Five guided touches were recorded at raw controller coordinates: top-left [216,17], top-right [215,470], bottom-right [14,468], bottom-left [7,20], center [119,266].
Both GPIO 12 and GPIO 0 produced clean press and release transitions on the exact final candidate.
The operator exercised edit, save, run, selected-app changes, and APP mode during qualification.
The exact final candidate returned HTTP 200 with text/html and the operator confirmed that the IDE loaded correctly.
Corrupt-hash, truncated-TAR, pre-staging low-space, post-manifest low-space, and forced-write failures failed closed without advancing the committed version.
A forced write failure left a durable failed marker and was recoverable without applying the target package.
Power was removed at the solid-white signal immediately after the durable install marker.
The old committed v0.14 state remained intact and the TartLab-Recovery access point served the correct interrupted-update diagnostic.
Retry normal boot restored a healthy IDE for the marker-present case.
A bandwidth-limited transfer was physically interrupted during tartlab.tar; the server recorded a connection reset and the device retained only manifest.json plus tartlab.tar.part.
No durable install marker or target directory was created and the old version remained committed.

The protected v0.13 recovery runtime re-enters recovery if Retry normal boot is selected while the legacy manifest remains. For this pre-marker case, the supported action is Install latest corrective release.

The exact final candidate was staged through that corrective-release path, committed only after a healthy IDE boot, removed the stale legacy manifest, and completed a second reboot directly into healthy IDE.
Clean installations include the corrected Retry normal boot cleanup; migrated devices gain the post-corrective-update cleanup through tartlabutils.tar.
The exact final candidate was fully staged and installation was physically interrupted at RECOVERY_POWER_SIGNAL=tartlabutils.tar.
The artifact server was stopped before the board was reconnected.
Offline resume recognized and skipped nine completed packages, installed only tartlabutils.tar, and returned v0.14.
The subsequent boot committed healthy v0.14 with zero failures, no update marker, and an empty recovery staging directory.
Application selector, hardware selector, device configuration, settings, logs, selected-app state, and user-file ownership were preserved across the applicable migrations and recovery paths.
User edits made during browser qualification remained present after corrective recovery and offline resume.
A descriptive follow-up OTA committed only after health and a same-version v0.14 OTA restored the intended release state.
After corrective recovery, a second boot and the final post-resume boot both reached healthy IDE with zero consecutive failures.

candidate_binding_notes: The exact final CI candidate was physically installed through corrective recovery, resumed offline after a real power cut, booted healthy, and received the final display, touch, button, HTTP, and human browser-load checks.

Fault-injection and the first two physical power cuts began on precursor candidates. The only later source changes were the recovery retry cleanup and post-corrective-health legacy manifest cleanup; their affected paths were repeated on the exact final candidate.
No promotion or GitHub release was performed during qualification.
